Architecture Note: Waypoint Dispatch Service Decomposition

The Dispatch Service is the application service the Waypoint web console and mobile app both call to place a job with a technician. It is realized by the Dispatch Component, the deployable application component that owns dispatch logic. The Dispatch Component accesses the Job Assignment, the data object that records which technician a job went to, and it is assigned to the Routing Function, the application function that chooses a technician for a job. The Routing Function also realizes the Dispatch Service and accesses the Job Assignment data object when it needs a technician's current load.

Callers never touch the component directly. The Dispatch Component provides the Dispatch API, the application interface everything else integrates against; that interface serves the Dispatch Service and depends on the Dispatch Component behind it.

End to end, placing and confirming a job is the Job Assignment Process, an application process that delivers value to the Dispatch Service. That process depends on the Routing Function to pick the technician and depends on the Dispatch API to commit the choice.

The Dispatch Component does not work alone: it uses the Notification Component, a second application component that pushes the assignment to the technician's handset. We model the pair as the Waypoint Dispatch Collaboration, an application collaboration that aggregates the Dispatch Component, provides the Dispatch API, and delivers value to the Dispatch Service the two components jointly stand up.
